audit.whatIsWrong: The reflect is called 'her R' in seven places. It is Rebuttal (W). Mel's R is Golden Eclipse, a global execute-style strike, and the matchup never names a single one of her abilities.
audit.why: Rebuttal is a 38/35/33/29/26s barrier that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker AND prevents her from taking damage. Golden Eclipse is 120/100/80s at 25000 range — it hits every enemy carrying Overwhelm stacks anywhere on the map. Telling a player to 'hold through her R' points them at the wrong ability and the wrong cooldown by a factor of three.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal named as W with its 38-second rank-1 cooldown; Golden Eclipse named as the global R; Radiant Volley, Solar Snare and Searing Brilliance named where they act.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] and whys[3] are one stage out of place — the Level 3 slot describes the pre-Mist dead zone and the Levels 4-5 slot describes level 6 — and the chart then gives Gwen Levels 4-5 (which the spike calls a 'dead zone') and gives Mel Level 6 (which the spike calls the flip).
audit.why: Mist is the pivot: Levels 4-5 are Mel's last good window and 6 is where Gwen takes over.
audit.corrected: whys re-slotted; chart set to Mel / Skill / Gwen / Mel / Gwen / Gwen / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and the reflect window is described as something to 'stay patient through' with no idea how long the punish lasts.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38 seconds at rank 1 — by far the longest basic cooldown in the lane, so a baited Rebuttal is most of a wave. Radiant Volley is 10s, Solar Snare 11s, Golden Eclipse 120s.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to the whys, mid, late and the cooldown breakdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Needlework is a projectile and Rebuttal reflects projectiles, or that Overwhelm stacks feed a global ultimate.
audit.why: Needlework is Gwen's only ranged tool and it is flagged projectile — thrown into Rebuttal it comes back at you. And Searing Brilliance stacks Overwhelm on everything Mel damages, executes at enough stacks, and Golden Eclipse then hits every marked target regardless of distance, so backing off low with stacks on you is not safe.
audit.corrected: Both stated in Key Ability Interactions and the late paragraph.

edits.after: Radiant Volley (Q, 10s) still out-ranges you and you have no Mist — last-hit at cone range and bank the wave instead of trading.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your soft spot — still no Hallowed Mist untargetability and pre-first-item, so her Q whittles you while you farm; respect it and don't force a bad all-in. At 6 it flips: dash in and drop Mist so she can't target you with ranged Q from outside it, then keep snipping her down in melee where her kit is weakest. The key with her R is timing, not Mist — never dump your autos or Q into the reflect window, since it bounces your own %-HP damage back; hold, let it expire, then unload while your passive heals the poke.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your soft spot — no Hallowed Mist untargetability and pre-first-item, so Radiant Volley (Q, 10s) whittles you while you farm; respect it and do not force. At 6 it flips: dash in and drop Mist so she cannot target you from outside it, then keep snipping in the melee her kit hates. Rebuttal is about timing, not Mist — it blocks damage AND reflects projectiles, so never dump autos, Q or a Needlework into it. Hold, let it expire, and you have 38 seconds at rank 1 to work with.

edits.before: You own the straight 1v1 all game — she's a squishy mage with no dash and you out-sustain her poke, so a single clean E-in under Mist kills her once you have Riftmaker. The only thing she earns respect for is her R reflect: never channel your full combo into it, or you eat your own %-HP burst. Stay patient through the reflect, keep her in melee range where Mist denies her poke, and close the lane before her zone control and execute start mattering in grouped fights.
edits.after: You own the straight 1v1 all game — a squishy mage with no dash, and you out-sustain her poke, so one clean E-in under Mist kills her once Riftmaker lands. Two things earn respect. Rebuttal reflects projectiles, so a Needlework thrown into it comes back at you. And Searing Brilliance stacks Overwhelm on everything she touches, which Golden Eclipse then cashes in from anywhere on the map — walking away low and marked is not the same as being safe.

edits.before: Track Mel's Solar Snare: Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. When it is down — Q-snip in the mist.
edits.after: Rebuttal (W, 38s at rank 1) blocks damage and REFLECTS projectiles — a Needlework thrown into it comes back at you.

edits.before: - Mel Solar Snare: matchup-defining — Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rebuttal (W): 38/35/33/29/26s — the longest cooldown in the lane; bait it and the next 38 seconds are yours. - Radiant Volley (Q): 10s. - Solar Snare (E): 11s, the root that sets up everything. - Golden Eclipse (R): 120s and global.

notes: How many Overwhelm stacks are needed for the passive execute is not in the kit file, so the text says 'enough stacks' rather than a number. Also unresolved: whether Rebuttal reflecting Needlework returns all three needle casts or only the one in flight — not answerable from Riot's text.
